full_story_outline.beginning: Maya receives written notice that the small venue's private lease will end after the weekend. Ellis, who owns the building, has a replacement tenant ready and will hear a documented extension offer only before Monday morning. Maya publicly promises one final show, even though ticket revenue alone cannot cover the requested deposit.
full_story_outline.development: Maya persuades performers and a neighborhood business to back the show. She chooses written commitments rather than hopeful social posts. Ellis points out that several commitments are conditional, which leaves Maya short of the cash proof he asked for.
full_story_outline.escalation: To close the gap, Maya puts her savings at risk and tells performers she can cover their fees. A sponsor then withdraws. Maya must admit that her promise to performers now depends on the same savings she offered to Ellis.
full_story_outline.major_reversal: Ellis offers a brief extension if Maya can deliver the deposit by morning, but only if she accepts a higher monthly payment. The offer turns her apparent victory into a new risk: the venue could survive the week and fail the next month.
full_story_outline.crisis: Maya can hide the new terms and collect support for a deal she doubts, or disclose them and risk losing the crowd's backing. She tells performers and supporters the exact terms and offers refunds to anyone who wants out.
full_story_outline.climax: After hearing the true cost, enough supporters keep their commitments to fund the deposit. Maya declines Ellis's first terms and proposes a shorter trial extension with a published revenue checkpoint. Ellis accepts that narrower risk over his uncertain replacement tenant.
full_story_outline.resolution: The venue opens for a limited trial period. Maya documents the money owed to performers and admits that keeping the room permanently remains unresolved; the new agreement gives the group a real deadline and a measurable next decision.
